<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains a standard source definition pointing to a GitHub release asset (geosite.dat) with a provided SHA256 checksum. This is a typical prebuilt binary artifact from a well-known public repository (Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat). The `sha256sums` field is populated (not SKIPped), which means the integrity of the downloaded file will be verified during installation—even though `--nobuild` skips the build phase, the checksum validation still occurs as part of the standard packaging process.

The `latestver()` function uses `gh api` to query the GitHub API for the latest version tag. This is a read-only operation that does not download or execute any external code—it simply retrieves metadata from the upstream repository. The `package()` function only installs the extracted file. No malicious code is introduced by either `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, as both commands operate within the bounds of the existing PKGBUILD without executing untrusted payloads.

All components align with standard AUR packaging practices: a pinned prebuilt artifact with a valid checksum, a straightforward version detection function, and no unexpected side effects. The source URL is publicly accessible and the checksum ensures authenticity.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>The source is a standard prebuilt artifact from a public GitHub release with a provided SHA256 checksum; the top-level `latestver()` function only queries the GitHub API for version metadata. Both `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` are standard build commands that do not execute malicious code.</summary>
